findings.evidence: Three cases share one missing binding from accepted markup to executed conditioning. (1) spanTokens encodes each stretch separately; chatTokens also renders a sentinel instead of the actual prompt. BPE is not additive: an admitted byte-level vocabulary a/b/ab with merge a b encodes clean ab as one token, while (a:1)b takes two independent encodes. Weight one can therefore change token IDs/conditioning before attention. Existing fake word-count encoders cannot catch this; graph-only weights-of-one checks do not prove input equivalence. (2) AssemblePaddedSequence places suffix at prefix+maximum-suffixLen, overwriting the final suffixLen prompt slots when full. rowWeights copies maximum weights without that boundary. The retained prefix3/budget5/suffix1 layout puts suffix at row7, but a fifth prompt weight2 gives that suffix weight2; Krea consumes this attended row. (3) MOSS accepts and strips markup from negative prompts through input, but only request.Prompt supplies settings.weights; load(name, negative, skip) passes none. Negative weights are silently discarded. These are source-admitted cases, not measured model-output failures.

findings.evidence:
record posts /prompt and receives prompt_id, then awaits history, derives timing and only then creates the output directory. The sole JSON write is after every /view download. An out path that is already a regular file fails after the remote job finishes; a transient history/view failure likewise returns recording{} with no durable prompt ID. Reinvoking the command unconditionally posts a new prompt, even if the accepted job completed. keep writes into the final section folder before the recording commits, so a failed retry can overwrite files still referenced by an older successful record. It also names files only by normalized node ID and basename: same-node outputs with the same basename in different source subfolders/kinds can alias. Current fake-server cases cover success and remote execution error, not local output failure or recovery. These are source-established admitted paths, not new remote runs.
SQA-389 (7daa461d05051a53bceb25d5ae05a66e2c2c096e): await starts from Devices[0].Total-Free and takes the maximum of later snapshots. main polls once per second and prints at most N bytes; the JSON calls it peak_card_bytes. A prompt can use more memory between polls and complete before the next stats read; await returns immediately on completed history, so the unsampled maximum is absent. The snapshots are whole-device usage, include preexisting/other-process allocations and choose device0, with no prompt-specific attribution. The fake fixture validates a known sampled maximum of700, not an upper bound on actual run peak. No measured hardware discrepancy or downstream admission decision is asserted.

findings.recommended_change:
Keep recorder.record as the remote-run owner and reuse its recording plus existing atomic JSON/directory publication. Admit the local destination before POST. Persist request/server/source binding and the accepted prompt ID immediately, then resume that ID through the existing history/view calls after interruption. Separate accepted/incomplete from complete records; do not repost an unchanged accepted request. If acceptance is uncertain, retain that uncertainty rather than claiming exactly-once execution or blindly resubmitting. Publish a complete fresh result set only after collection, protecting a prior successful record and unique file identities; preserve node/kind/subfolder identity or content addressing through the existing owner. Use the same recording, not a second notes ledger, scheduler, daemon or retry framework.
Keep the existing snapshots if useful, but represent and display them explicitly as maximum observed whole-device usage over the polling window, with device/cadence/source and unknown actual run peak. Remove the at-most claim. Only claim a true per-run peak when the existing reference backend provides an attributable measurement; do not increase polling, subtract an arbitrary baseline or add instrumentation services merely to preserve the label. Preserve old record interpretation explicitly.
